query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A cryogenic deformation treatment (cryo-rolling) followed by a controlled annealing step reduces dislocation pile-ups at the lamellar colony internal boundaries of the eutectic high-entropy alloy, thereby mitigating local stress concentrations that lead to microcracking, and results in simultaneous enhancement of room-temperature tensile ductility and strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with hierarchical microstructure featuring dual-phase lamellar colonies exhibiting coarse phase boundaries that serve as sites for dislocation pile-up and microcrack initiation.
generation.intervention: Apply cryogenic rolling (cryo-deformation) to the alloy followed by a controlled annealing process.
generation.conditions: Process performed at cryogenic temperatures during deformation and annealing under conditions tuned to achieve partial recrystallization; tensile tests performed at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a refined, nano-lamellar microstructure with ultrafine grains in the FCC lamellae and reduced coarseness of the B2 phase, which collectively redistribute strain more uniformly and minimize dislocation accumulations at internal boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The cryo-rolling step forces dislocations to be introduced under low-temperature conditions, which, when followed by controlled annealing, leads to controlled recovery and recrystallization that refines the microstructure. This refined structure reduces the spacing of internal boundaries and hindering potential sites for dislocation pile-up, thus lowering local stress concentrations that lead to microcracking and catastrophic failure.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in both yield strength and tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy. Strength is expected to be maintained or increased (similar to or above approximately 1437 MPa yield strength as observed in processed HEAs), and ductility (elongation to failure) is expected to be improved toward or above 14%, compared to the baseline brittle behavior at room temperature.
generation.baseline: Untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy exhibiting brittle behavior due to dislocation pile-ups near the coarse internal boundaries of the lamellar microstructure.
generation.boundary: This intervention is applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies; its efficacy may vary with the specific alloy chemistry, initial cast microstructure, and exact processing parameters (deformation strain levels, cryogenic temperature, and annealing temperature and time).
generation.uncertainty: While prior work supports the concurrent improvement in strength and ductility using cryo-deformation and annealing, precise processing parameters (rolling strain, annealing schedule) required to achieve optimal microstructural refinement have inherent uncertainty and may need further optimization for specific alloys.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of the eutectic high-entropy alloy and subject them to the cryo-rolling followed by controlled annealing intervention. A set of control samples should remain unprocessed. Ensure that the processing parameters are carefully documented. Perform standardized room-temperature tensile tests on all samples.
measurements: Microstructural characterization (grain size, lamellar spacing, phase distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in both ductility (elongation to failure) and yield strength compared to the untreated alloy, or if microcrack initiation and propagation (associated with dislocation pile-ups) are not reduced as evidenced in microstructural analyses, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Simultaneous Strength-Ductility Enhancement of a Nano-Lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 Eutectic High Entropy Alloy by Cryo-Rolling and Annealing

Abstract: Nano-lamellar (L12 + B2) AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA) was processed by cryo-rolling and annealing. The EHEA developed a novel hierarchical microstructure featured by fine lamellar regions consisting of FCC lamellae filled with ultrafine FCC grains (average size ~200–250 nm) and B2 lamellae, and coarse non-lamellar regions consisting of ultrafine FCC (average size ~200–250 nm), few coarse recrystallized FCC grains and rather coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase (~2.5 µm). This complex and hierarchical microstructure originated from differences in strain-partitioning amongst the constituent phases, affecting the driving force for recrystallization. The hierarchical microstructure of the cryo-rolled and annealed material resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength (Yield Strength/YS: 1437 ± 26 MPa, Ultimate Tensile Strength/UTS: 1562 ± 33 MPa) and ductility (elongation to failure/ef ~ 14 ± 1%) as compared to the as-cast as well as cold-rolled and annealed materials.
